Goal `core-taint-and-1-more`: `Core\Taint` is complete, and so is `Core\Task::afterResponse` —
about, a Rust test beside the `.nvst` cases, three examples, one attack, one bench with its record,
and `Core\Task`'s class card, so `Core\Task` is off `CLASSES_STILL_OWING_A_CARD`. Its attack found
that a `deadline` of `0s` or less on `afterResponse` meant no deadline at all; fixed in
`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/task.rs`'s `nvs_core_task_after_response` and pinned by
`tests/conformance/core/task-after-response-deadline-of-zero-or-less-is-already-over.nvst`.
`Core\Task::all` and `Core\Task::map` are untaken. Nothing is blocked.

items.text: **`Core\Task::all`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, tests, and a card rewritten in the plain voice the way `AFTER_RESPONSE_DOC` now is. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/task.rs:142`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/task.rs:213`
**`Core\Task::map`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, tests, and the same card rewrite. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/task.rs:151`, `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/task.rs:234`

backlog: A group `deadline` does not stop a child that never waits: `Core\Task::all({busy: …}, {deadline: 1ms})` over a 300-million-step `while` runs the loop to its end and throws `TimeoutError` after it, and `afterResponse` logs the timeout the same way. The deadline is noticed only where the child waits (`Core\Time::sleep`). Whether a group deadline should arm the back-edge poll that `[limits] wall_time` uses is a question for `rule:concurrency/nothing-is-still-running-when-a-call-returns`'s owner; the attacks written so far wait rather than spin, so none is gap-marked. Owning doc: `crates/nvs-runtime/src/deferred.rs`'s module doc.
